title: Realization compares homotopy classes into a Kan complex
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, geometric realization and the internal functor simplicial set of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe. For a simplicial set $S$, let $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(S)$ be its vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of edges. For topological spaces $A,B$, let $[A,B]_{\mathrm{top}}$ be the set of continuous maps $A\to B$ modulo continuous homotopies $A\times[0,1]\to B$, with ordinary product topology and with no basepoint fixed. For every simplicial set $K$ and Kan complex $W$, geometric realization of maps induces a bijection
$$\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,W)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }[|K|,|W|]_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad [a]\longmapsto[|a|].$$
This bijection is natural under precomposition by every simplicial map $K'\to K$ and postcomposition by every simplicial map between Kan targets. Neither $K$ nor $W$ is required to be nonempty, and $K$ need not be Kan.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2 (Tag 0149), on components, with Construction 3.6.5.1 (Tag 0148) Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; no Stacks tag for this comparison theorem was found.

proof.text: Put $T=|W|$ and define $V=\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ with $V_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$ and affine-precomposition operators. The realization adjunction of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] applies: $T$ is a k-space, since it is a realization. Its horn-pair assertion identifies $|\Lambda_i^n|\subseteq|\Delta^n|$ with $D^{n-1}\times\{0\}\subseteq D^{n-1}\times[0,1]$ for every $n\geq1$ and every $i$, including the outer horns. The projection $(z,t)\mapsto(z,0)$ gives a continuous retraction onto the horn. A map $\Lambda_i^n\to V$ is adjoint to a continuous map $|\Lambda_i^n|\to T$; precompose the latter with this retraction and take its adjoint to obtain a filler $\Delta^n\to V$. Hence $V$ is Kan. No condition in dimension zero has been used.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2, singular Kan assertion; horn-pair and adjunction input expanded explicitly

proof.text: The characteristic-map unit $u=u_W:W\to V$ sends $w\in W_n$ to $t\mapsto[w,t]$. By [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak], $|u|$ induces a bijection on path components and all based homotopy-group isomorphisms. The hypothesis already says $W$ is Kan, and step 1 proves $V$ is Kan. Apply [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] to obtain $v:V\to W$ and simplicial homotopies $vu\simeq\mathrm{id}_W$ and $uv\simeq\mathrm{id}_V$, with cylinders $W\times\Delta^1$ and $V\times\Delta^1$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2, unit-map argument, using Theorem 3.6.4.1 and Proposition 3.1.7.13

proof.text: Postcomposition with $u$ and $v$ gives inverse maps on edge-generated classes of maps from $K$. Indeed an edge $h:K\times\Delta^1\to W$ is taken to $uh$, and similarly for $v$; thus both maps respect the generating relation and its equivalence closure. If $a:K\to W$, precomposing the homotopy $vu\simeq\mathrm{id}_W$ with $a\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}$ gives an edge between $vua$ and $a$. The homotopy $uv\simeq\mathrm{id}_V$ does the same for each $b:K\to V$. Therefore $u_*:\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,W)\to\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,V)$ is a bijection, inverse to $v_*$. This uses only the degreewise Fun and product definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], not homotopy invariance under a weak equivalence of source shapes.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.5.2, postcomposition with the chosen homotopy inverse, written on edges

proof.text: By the adjunction in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], actual simplicial maps $b:K\to V$ are in bijection with continuous maps $\bar b:|K|\to T$. Explicitly $\bar b([k,t])=b_n(k)(t)$; the simplicial equation makes this independent of the quotient representative, and the quotient topology proves continuity. Conversely a continuous $F:|K|\to T$ gives $b_n(k)(t)=F([k,t])$. Apply the same adjunction to $K\times\Delta^1$. The homeomorphism $\rho_K:|K\times\Delta^1|\cong|K|\times[0,1]$ and its endpoint formulas in [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] identify edges between $b_0,b_1$ with continuous homotopies between $\bar b_0,\bar b_1$, in both directions. Continuous homotopy of maps is already an equivalence relation: use a constant interval, reverse $t\mapsto1-t$, and concatenate two homotopies by their formulas at $2t$ and $2t-1$ on the two closed half-intervals; they agree at the midpoint, so the pasted map is continuous. Consequently the actual-map bijection descends to a bijection $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,V)\cong[|K|,T]_{\mathrm{top}}$. The cylinder theorem uses the ordinary product topology, exactly as required in the statement.

source.place: Example 3.6.2.5 on vertices and edges; Construction 3.6.5.1, with the ordinary cylinder theorem

proof.text: Compose the bijections of steps 3 and 4. For $a:K\to W$ the map $u a$ has adjoint $[k,t]\mapsto u_n(a_n(k))(t)=[a_n(k),t]$, which is exactly $|a|$. Thus this composite is the asserted map, with no unspecified comparison. If $r:K'\to K$ and $s:W\to W'$ is a simplicial map to another Kan complex, its two naturality composites both send $[a]$ to the class of the continuous map $[k',t]\mapsto[s_n(a_n(r_n(k'))),t]$; hence both naturality squares commute. These compositions preserve homotopies by composing a homotopy with $|r|\times\mathrm{id}_{[0,1]}$ and $|s|$. Finally, if $K=\varnothing$, both sides have one element (the empty map). If $W=\varnothing$ and $K\ne\varnothing$, both sides are empty: a nonempty simplicial set has a vertex by face restriction and a nonempty realization. If both are empty the first case applies. These cases also satisfy the formulas above. No Kan property of $K$ or chosen basepoint was used.

(2) The unit node's conclusion is exactly the Whitehead node's hypothesis, and both Kan hypotheses are in force. (3) Postcomposing the cylinder homotopies H, J with a x id gives edges, so u_* and v_* are inverse. (5) The adjoint of u.a is |a|; naturality holds; the cases K empty, W empty and K=W=point are checked. lean.statement: theorem kan_realization_mapping_classes : ∃ e : ∀ (K W : SSet.{u}) [KanComplex W], π₀ ((ihom K).obj W) ≃ Quot (@ContinuousMap.Homotopic |K| |W| _ _), (∀ (K W : SSet.{u}) [KanComplex W] (a : K ⟶ W), e K W (π₀.mk (diagramVertex a)) = Quot.mk _ (toTop.map a).hom) ∧ (∀ (K K' W : SSet.{u}) [KanComplex W] (r : K' ⟶ K) (x : π₀ ((ihom K).obj W)), e K' W (mapπ₀ ((MonoidalClosed.pre r).app W) x) = Quot.map (fun f : C(|K|, |W|) ↦ f.comp (toTop.map r).hom) (fun _ _ h ↦ h.comp (ContinuousMap.Homotopic.refl (toTop.map r).hom)) (e K W x)) ∧ (∀ (K W W' : SSet.{u}) [KanComplex W] [KanComplex W'] (s : W ⟶ W') (x : π₀ ((ihom K).obj W)), e K W' (mapπ₀ ((ihom K).map s) x) = Quot.map (fun f : C(|K|, |W|) ↦ (toTop.map s).hom.comp f) (fun _ _ h ↦ (ContinuousMap.Homotopic.refl (toTop.map s).hom).comp h) (e K W x))
lean.note: A single existential family of equivalences, fixed on every simplicial-map representative by geometric realization, with explicit precomposition and postcomposition naturality. Uses Mathlib edge components and the literal quotient by ContinuousMap.Homotopic; no comparison map is supplied as a hypothesis.
